counting: 270 executed checks include seven shared Chromium handshake cases repeated inside the 36-check integration suite. Counts represent suite executions, not 270 independent concepts. The isolated Edge test adds six real-browser cases; Firefox source is covered by VM/integration tests, not a live Firefox run.

deadlineContract.scope: Ordinary request budget includes startup, selection validation and acknowledgement. Capture status retains one safe retry within a two-attempt total budget. Shared protocol warmup can finish for another request after an earlier request expires, but the expired request cannot dispatch.

cancellationContract: Explicit disconnect rejects live requests waiting on validation, startup, persistent acknowledgements or legacy one-shot replies. Checks after awaits and after beforeSend prevent a late callback from reconnecting or posting. Dispatched mutations never retry automatically; capture-status alone retains its existing safe read retry.
coverage: Legacy lost acknowledgement returns uncertainty once, ignores late success and does not replay
Persistent and legacy validation hangs time out before dispatch; late validation cannot send
A short request budget does not close another request shared startup
Startup plus acknowledgement obeys the total mutation budget
Disconnect during validation/legacy wait and reentrant beforeSend cannot post an abandoned command
Existing capture-status retry, media receipts and browser ownership transaction checks remain green
browserFixtureNotes: Actual Edge native messaging and actual 7.60 host; only static hello messages. Legacy negotiation and reply stalls are deliberately injected around those real APIs. sent in the raw record counts beforeSend callbacks; wire/oneShot identify actual outbound metadata messages. This does not test a public video or file download.
limits: No personal browser, YouTube/ad capture, File Info paint or final video-file acceptance in this increment

Timer-based deadlines do not establish hard real-time latency

Native runtime logic is unchanged from 7.58 except version metadata; no claim that the earlier native suites were rerun as 7.60
